## Background

Pilot Wnet is an open studio controller (ESP32-S3, W5500 Ethernet, USB-C, LoRa). The Rev A schematic and layout were generated by Python scripts (using SKiDL, Freerouting and a custom raster router) that AI agents wrote and ran. ERC and DRC report 0 errors, but no engineer has assessed the layout. An AI-agent audit (Claude agents, 20 Nov 2026, measurements taken from the board file; not reviewed by an engineer) found these defects; the IDs refer to the audit summary in `docs/AUDYT_REV_A.md` (Polish):

1. Most signals run on the inner layers (In1 GND, In2 +3V3), while B.Cu is almost empty. Under the W5500 the In1 ground covers only 39% of the package outline (layout-01, zasilanie-15).
2. The buck converter U3 (TLV62569) is placed against the TI datasheet: the input capacitor is far from the IC, the SW node is long, and the FB trace runs under the SW node (zasilanie-01, layout-02).
3. The 25 MHz crystal Y1 has bad XO routing: the XO trace from the W5500 to Y1 makes a 17.6 mm detour through 4 vias (via R58 and C41) and runs on In2 directly under the crystal; LoRa SPI traces run on In1 under it. XI (5.1 mm) is fine (layout-04).
4. ESD protection is far from the connectors: for 6 of the 10 inputs the SRV05-4 channel is 46–66 mm (straight line) from its connector, because channels follow list order, not placement; the input traces are up to 93 mm long, mostly on In1 (zasilanie-02, interfejsy-04).
5. The Ethernet traces from the W5500 to the RJ45 are not routed as differential pairs over continuous ground: the halves run on different layers, with length mismatches of 11 mm and 4.6 mm (layout-05, interfejsy-05).

### The board

- KiCad 10.0.8 (board and project files; the schematic is written by `pcb/schemat.py` in an older format), 4 layers: F.Cu signals, In1 GND, In2 +3V3, B.Cu signals; 90 × 100 mm, 1.6 mm, default JLCPCB stack-up.
- JLCPCB assembly: all SMD parts on top, a few THT parts (RJ45, JST XH, 2.54 mm headers); about 128 placed parts, 43 BOM lines with LCSC part numbers.
- Main blocks:
  - ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8; the module is flush with the top edge, and its PCB antenna lies over the board with a copper keep-out on all four layers (Espressif recommends the antenna beyond the edge or a cut-out; consider it in Rev B, layout-12);
  - WIZnet W5500 (LQFP-48, 0.5 mm pitch), 25 MHz crystal, RJ45 HR911105A with integrated magnetics;
  - TI TLV62569 buck converter, 5 V → 3.3 V;
  - USB-C with fuse, TVS and USBLC6;
  - Ebyte E22-900M22S LoRa module, 868 MHz, soldered by hand, antenna through the module's IPEX connector;
  - I2C (OLED, Qwiic);
  - 10 button and joystick inputs on JST XH connectors, with RC filters and SRV05-4 ESD arrays;
  - 74LVC1G04 inverter.
- Files: `pcb/kicad/pilot_wnet.kicad_pro`, `.kicad_sch`, `.kicad_pcb`, `.kicad_dru`; project library in `pcb/lib/`. Background in Polish: `pcb/README.md`, `pcb/v01/README_v01.md`, `DECYZJE.md`, `docs/AUDYT_REV_A.md`.

## Scope

- Review the current placement and re-place the critical blocks: the W5500 with its crystal, the buck converter, the USB protection and the ESD diodes. Connector positions do not change (see Constraints).
- Route the board so that it meets K1–K12. You may start from scratch or from the current layout.
- Re-assign the channels of the SRV05-4 arrays (U10–U12) to the nearest connectors and update the schematic; ERC must still report 0 errors.
- Net classes and design rules: compute the impedance of the Ethernet and USB pairs with the JLCPCB impedance calculator for the chosen stack-up; the rules must stay within JLCPCB capabilities.
- Redraw the E22-900M22S symbol and footprint from the Ebyte datasheet (the current ones come from the EasyEDA/LCSC library and cannot stay, see `NOTICE.md`); keep the pad coordinates so the routing still fits, and check pin 12 (NRST according to Ebyte, tied to GND in Rev A, interfejsy-08).
- Silkscreen: add "CERN-OHL-S-2.0" and the repository URL (the Source Location from `NOTICE.md`).
- Nice to have: test points (pads on F.Cu) for 3V3, 5V, GND, EN, TXD0 and RXD0.
- If you find a schematic or footprint error (for example, check the USB-C footprint J1 against the HRO datasheet), report it here; it will be fixed after agreement. Other open schematic findings are listed in `docs/AUDYT_REV_A.md` (for example J20 vs. a standard FTDI cable, +5 V on pin 3 of J10–J15, D1 vs. the 6 V limit of U3).

**Source of truth.** From Rev B the KiCad project is planned to become the source of truth, and the SKiDL generator would remain only as a netlist regression check. The maintainers will confirm this here before work starts.

## Constraints

Change these only after agreement in this issue.

- The 90 × 100 mm outline, the mounting holes H1–H4 and the connector positions are frozen to the Rev A board (K11): USB-C (J1), RJ45 (J2), JST XH (J10–J16), OLED and Qwiic (J17, J18), headers J19 and J20, and the LoRa module footprint. The enclosure files (`projekt/arcade.toml`) still assume a 100 × 100 mm board and older cut-outs; they will be updated to match the board.
- All parts stay on the top side.
- Project rules (more conservative than JLCPCB's 4-layer minimums): track and space at least 0.15/0.15 mm, vias at least 0.3 mm drill and 0.6 mm diameter, copper-to-edge clearance per JLCPCB.
- BOM unchanged (JLCPCB/LCSC stock parts). Part or package swaps only after agreement.
- GPIO assignment unchanged unless agreed: a change requires firmware changes (`firmware/micropython/lib/konfig_plytki.py`).

## Acceptance criteria

The CI workflow (`.github/workflows/kicad.yml`) checks the automatic part of K1: ERC 0 errors; DRC 0 errors, 0 unconnected items and 0 schematic-parity issues. Whether the remaining warnings are documented, and K2–K12, are checked by review and geometry measurement.

- [ ] **K1. ERC and DRC.** DRC in KiCad 10 with schematic parity: 0 errors, 0 unconnected items, 0 schematic-parity issues, and only warnings that are documented. ERC: 0 errors.
- [ ] **K2. Planes.** In1 is one continuous GND zone and In2 is the +3V3 zone. There is not a single track segment on In1 or In2.
  - Cut-outs are allowed only in the ESP32 antenna keep-out and, if justified, under the line side of the RJ45.
  - Islands of other voltages on In2 only after agreement. No fast signal (W5500 SPI, differential pairs, crystal) crosses an island boundary.
- [ ] **K3. Ground under the W5500.** In1 ground copper covers at least 90% of the W5500 outline (today 39%).
- [ ] **K4. Crystal Y1.**
  - The XI and XO traces are each at most 5 mm long, from crystal pad to W5500 pin.
  - No vias on these nets.
  - The load capacitors sit next to the crystal.
  - No other signals under Y1 or its traces, on F.Cu or B.Cu.
- [ ] **K5. Buck converter U3**, laid out per section 10 (Layout) of the TLV62569 datasheet:
  - input capacitor at most 2 mm (pad to pad) from the VIN and GND pins, on F.Cu, no vias in the input loop;
  - inductor at the SW pin; the SW node only on F.Cu and no longer than 3 mm;
  - output capacitor at the inductor;
  - FB divider at the FB pin; the FB trace does not run under the inductor or the SW node on any layer;
  - power ground connected to In1 with at least 4 vias.
- [ ] **K6. Ethernet.** TXP/TXN and RXP/RXN from the W5500 to the RJ45 are routed as differential pairs:
  - only on F.Cu, over continuous In1 ground, without vias;
  - differential impedance 100 Ω ±10% for the JLCPCB stack-up, with the geometry stored in the net class;
  - length difference within a pair at most 0.5 mm;
  - spacing to other nets at least 3 × the track width;
  - termination parts near the W5500, as in the WIZnet reference design.
- [ ] **K7. USB.**
  - D+ and D− as a 90 Ω ±10% pair on F.Cu;
  - U2 (USBLC6) at most 5 mm from J1;
  - fuse and TVS between the connector and the rest of the circuit.
- [ ] **K8. ESD diodes.**
  - Each SRV05-4 channel sits at its nearest connector.
  - The trace from the connector pin to the diode is at most 15 mm (today up to ~90 mm of trace; 46–66 mm straight line for 6 inputs).
  - Order along the trace: connector → diode → RC filter.
  - The diode's GND pin connects to In1 through a via at most 1 mm from the pad.

  If the connector spacing makes this impossible for the three arrays, say so in stage 1.
- [ ] **K9. No via-in-pad** on SMD pads. Exception: the thermal vias in the U1 footprint from the project library.
- [ ] **K10. Antenna keep-out.** The area under the ESP32 antenna stays free of copper, tracks and vias on all four layers, as today.
- [ ] **K11. Mechanics.** Connectors and holes stay exactly where they are today (coordinates identical to the current board, 0.00 mm difference). All parts on the top side.
- [ ] **K12. Fabrication files** are generated from the delivered version of the project and complete per the list below.

## Deliverables

Delivered as a pull request to this repository; large generated outputs (Gerbers, PDFs, STEP) may be attached to the pull request or a release instead of being committed.

1. KiCad 10 project: `.kicad_pro`, `.kicad_sch`, `.kicad_pcb` and `.kicad_dru` files, and the project library with footprints and 3D models.
2. ERC and DRC reports from kicad-cli (text or JSON).
3. Files for JLCPCB:
   - Gerbers of all layers, including the outline;
   - Excellon drill files (PTH and NPTH);
   - BOM and placement (CPL) files in JLCPCB format, with rotation corrections;
   - stack-up name and impedance parameters for the order.
4. Drawings and 3D: PDF of the copper layers, assembly drawing, STEP of the assembled board for checking against the enclosure.
5. A short design note (Markdown, 1–3 pages, English or Polish) for the open hardware documentation, covering:
   - stack-up and impedances;
   - net classes;
   - block placement and the reasons for it;
   - buck converter, Ethernet and ESD;
   - schematic changes;
   - deviations from the criteria, with reasons;
   - which steps were done by automated tools or AI, and which by a person.
6. One round of fixes after review.

## Stages

1. **Placement** of the critical blocks. Post screenshots and files here, or open a draft pull request, for review before routing.
2. **Routing** and a check against K1–K12.
3. **Fabrication files and design note**, followed by one review round.

Work in the open from the first commit: open a draft pull request early.

## How to apply

Comment here or start a thread in Discussions with:

- a link to a KiCad project of yours under an open licence;
- an example of a board with Ethernet or with 4 layers (layer screenshots or a portfolio), and your role in it;
- how you would route the Ethernet (100 Ω) and USB (90 Ω) pairs on the JLCPCB 4-layer, 1.6 mm stack-up (approximate track width and gap), and how you would handle the planes under an RJ45 with integrated magnetics;
- the tools you use (kicad-cli, Python, KiCad IPC API, MCP, AI agents) and what you check by hand;
- whether you agree to work in the open from the first commit under CERN-OHL-S-2.0.

Details of paid work (estimate per stage, milestones, contract) are arranged after this first contact in Discussions.
